newsitem.title: USA: US swap spreads mostly steady, eyes on 10-years.
newsitem.headline: US swap spreads mostly steady, eyes on 10-years.

text.p: U.S. interest rate swap spreads were mostly steady in relatively calm trade on Monday amid dimming prospects of an imminent Federal Reserve credit tightening, traders said.

The market's focus remained on the 10-year maturity, where spreads had widened last week on news that the U.S. Treasury would not hold 10-year note auctions as scheduled in July and October, they added.
"That's where most of the activity has been," said a U.S. bank trader in California.

He said 10-year spreads have been fluctuating fairly widely in the past month, tightening slightly about two weeks ago due to corporate bond issues and then bouncing back on concerns over tighter government note supply.
On Monday, 10-year spreads were quoted at about 36/37 basis points, where they have been since early last week, when they popped up about three bps in a matter of day or two.

"It's been pretty much dealers buying each other's positions until they reached a level where the increased estimated value of repo specials was priced into the market, and that looks to be about three bps," the trader said.
Traders said corporate bonds have had little impact on the market in recent days.

"It's been pinned at those levels ever since people started talking about the 10-year note supply and word actually came out from the Treasury," said a Japanese bank trader in New York. "I don't think there's been much interest on the corporate side."
At the shorter end of the curve, rates were little changed as the flow was largely dominated by day-to-day inter-dealer trades.
"It's more just book-management and probably some customer interest," said a European bank trader in New York. "It's nothing out of the ordinary, just back and forth all day long."
Two-year spreads were roughly unchanged from late last week at around 25/28 bps.
